body.zh-HK:
> 面試官問：「candidate renewal-risk model 喺 offline evaluation 勝過 baseline，但一星期後 reviewer 話工作冇好做咗。你會檢查乜？」
>
> 答啱一半嘅答案：「ranking metric 高咗，operations team 大概只係未適應。」

## 把系統拆開看

先把比較鎖在每個決定當刻可見的資料。即使只用 synthetic data，point-in-time split 也要把當時未存在的 snapshot 留作後測；後來才有的 outcome 或月尾欄位不可悄悄放進 training。用同一個 holdout queue，比較規則式或舊模型的 baseline 與 candidate。之後檢查 calibration：相近的 score 是否對應相近的實際可能性？Score 不是指令；threshold 要按 reviewer capacity 決定，例如每人每日能認真處理多少個 case。Offline ranking 較好，仍可能產生不可用的 queue：case mix 變了、borderline handoff 太多，或 reviewer 根本不知道為何要處理某個 case。

這條 queue 只是一個 workflow proxy：reviewer 收到可處理、有優先次序的清單，並可接受、拒絕或退回 case。它不是 retention、客戶得益或收入等真實 outcome 的證明。先用 shadow mode，保留 baseline queue，讓一位清楚命名的 human owner 作最終決定。監察 calibration、超出 capacity、handoff rate 和延遲才出現的 outcome。只有符合預先同意的 gate 才 release；一旦 guardrail 失效，就 rollback 到 baseline 或簡單規則。這仍是 synthetic demonstration，不可聲稱已有商業成果。

## 多搵到紅貼紙，不等於幫到老師

想像新貼紙分類機在測試箱找多了紅色貼紙。假如老師收到一大堆貼紙、唔知每張點解被揀中，或者根本冇時間檢查，它仍然幫唔到手。先確認它會交到一小疊真人可以用的貼紙。

## 你會在工作裡碰到它

這題測試你能否把 model evaluation 接上外面的真人系統。好答案會分開「可量度的 model proxy」與「真正的決定」，並說清楚 owner、capacity 和 stop rule，令系統可被交代。

## 這個練習交到的技術證據

- 用 synthetic data 做 point-in-time split，避免 future-data leakage。
- 對比 baseline 與 candidate、檢查 score calibration，並按 capacity 定 threshold。
- 保留有版本的 queue evidence 和 monitoring signal，支援 release 或 rollback 決定。

## 交付和風險怎樣處理

- 以 reviewer capacity 和可用 workflow 為中心，而不是只看分數 dashboard。
- 分開 workflow proxy 與延遲出現的真實 outcome。
- 設 human handoff、有責任人的 release gate、回到安全 baseline 的 rollback，以及明確 nonclaim。

## 答案容易漏掉的地方

不要把較高 AUROC 或 average precision 直接叫做「business value」，更不要由它自動派發行動。先做有 capacity 上限的規則式 queue 和人工 checklist；用 shadow mode 對比 candidate，並讓 reviewer 記錄每個建議是否真的可用。

## 你可帶去面試的證據

提交 synthetic-data card、point-in-time split rule、baseline/candidate report、calibration 與 threshold decision record、capacity simulation、reviewer handoff form、release/rollback checklist，以及「未觀察到真實續約 outcome」的明確聲明。

## 延伸閱讀

[Renewal Triage：考慮 capacity 的 ML Lab](/zh-HK/articles/renewal-triage-mlops)、[用證據而不是流暢度評 portfolio](/zh-HK/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency) 與 [把課程作業變成八星期能力證據 sprint](/zh-HK/articles/turn-an-ai-course-into-an-eight-week-evidence-sprint)。

## 90 秒之後，要交到甚麼

答完之後，自己追問三句：我講清楚哪個機制？我說明了哪個取捨或會停下來的 failure？我可以打開哪一件 artefact 讓人核對？若三句裡有一句只能靠口講，先補一個固定 case、短 trace、decision record 或 README 段落。

## 兩類證據，要分開講

**技術證據**可以是固定 input 的 expected result、版本化設定、測試、trace 或被拒絕的 case。它要證明你知道系統在哪裡失敗，而不只展示一個流暢輸出。

**交付、業務與風險證據**要說清楚誰使用結果、錯一次會阻礙哪個決定、誰可接手，以及系統明確不會做甚麼。portfolio 例子只用 synthetic data 或已授權 fixture；它不是任何公司系統、現時面試流程或商業成果的描述。

## 範圍說明

這是 AI.DOG 的單題練習。題目、情境、資料、artefact 和結果均為教學用途；不要把它當作某間公司的題目、產品行為或招聘預測。

先把比较锁在每个决策当下可见的数据。即使只用 synthetic data，point-in-time split 也要把当时尚未存在的 snapshot 留作后测；后来才有的 outcome 或月末字段不能悄悄放进 training。用同一个 holdout queue，对比规则式或旧模型的 baseline 与 candidate。接着检查 calibration：相近的 score 是否对应相近的实际可能性？Score 不是指令；threshold 必须按 reviewer capacity 决定，例如每人每天能认真处理多少个 case。Offline ranking 较好，仍可能产生不可用的 queue：case mix 改变、borderline handoff 太多，或 reviewer 根本不知道为什么要处理某个 case。

想像一台新的贴纸分类机在测试箱找到更多红色贴纸。假如老师收到一大堆贴纸、不知道每张为什么被选中，或根本没有时间检查，它仍然帮不上忙。先确认它能交出一小叠真人可以使用的贴纸。

这题测试你能否把 model evaluation 接到外面的真人系统。好答案会分开“可测量的 model proxy”与“真正的决策”，并说清楚 owner、capacity 与 stop rule，让系统可以被交代。

## 这个练习交出的技术证据

- 用 synthetic data 做 point-in-time split，避免 future-data leakage。
- 对比 baseline 与 candidate、检查 score calibration，并按 capacity 定 threshold。
- 保留有版本的 queue evidence 与 monitoring signal，支持 release 或 rollback 决策。

- 以 reviewer capacity 与可用 workflow 为中心，而不是只看分数 dashboard。
- 分开 workflow proxy 与延迟出现的真实 outcome。
- 设 human handoff、有责任人的 release gate、回到安全 baseline 的 rollback，以及明确 nonclaim。

## 答案容易遗漏的地方

不要把较高 AUROC 或 average precision 直接叫做“business value”，更不要由它自动派发行动。先做有 capacity 上限的规则式 queue 和人工 checklist；用 shadow mode 对比 candidate，并让 reviewer 记录每个建议是否真的可用。

**技术证据**可以是固定 input 的 expected result、版本化设置、测试、trace 或被拒绝的案例。它要证明你知道系统在哪里失败，而不是只展示一个流畅输出。

body.en:
> Interviewer asks: “Your candidate renewal-risk model beats the baseline offline. A week later, reviewers say it has not made their work better. What do you inspect?”
>
> Half-right answer: “The ranking metric improved, so the operations team probably needs more time to adapt.”

## Open the mechanism

Make the comparison time-safe first. Even with synthetic data, a point-in-time split must hold out the snapshots that were not available when each decision would have been made; a later outcome or end-of-month field cannot quietly enter training. Compare a rules-based or previous-model baseline and a candidate on the same held-out queue. Then check calibration: does a similar score correspond to a similar observed likelihood? A score is not an instruction. Its threshold must be chosen against finite reviewer capacity, such as the number of cases people can properly review per day. A better offline ranking can still produce an unusable queue if it changes the case mix, creates too many borderline handoffs, or hides why a reviewer should act.

The queue is only a workflow proxy: reviewers receive a feasible, prioritised list and can accept, reject or return cases. It is not proof of a real outcome such as retention, customer benefit or revenue. Start in shadow mode, retain the baseline queue, and let a named human owner make the decision. Monitor calibration, capacity overrun, handoff rate and delayed outcome availability. Release only against agreed gates; roll back to the baseline or a simple rule when a guardrail fails. This remains a synthetic demonstration, not a claim that a business outcome occurred.

## More red stickers do not automatically help the teacher

Suppose a new sticker sorter finds more red stickers in a test box. It still does not help if the teacher gets a huge pile, cannot tell why each sticker was picked, or has no time to check them. First see whether the sorter makes a small, useful pile for a real person.

## Where this shows up at work

This tests whether you can join model evaluation to the human system around it. A strong answer separates a measurable model proxy from the actual decision and names the person, capacity and stop rule that make the system accountable.

## The technical work on show

- Synthetic, point-in-time data splits that avoid future-data leakage.
- A baseline-versus-candidate comparison, score calibration and a capacity-aware threshold.
- Versioned queue evidence and monitoring signals that can support a release or rollback decision.

## The delivery and risk work on show

- Reviewer capacity and a usable workflow rather than a score-only dashboard.
- The boundary between a workflow proxy and a delayed real-world outcome.
- Human handoff, an accountable release gate, rollback to a safe baseline and an explicit nonclaim.

## Where an answer goes thin

Do not call a higher AUROC or average precision “business value”, and do not automatically assign an action from it. Begin with a capacity-limited rules queue and a manual checklist; compare the candidate in shadow mode while reviewers record whether each recommendation was usable.

## Evidence you can point to

Commit a synthetic-data card, point-in-time split rule, baseline/candidate report, calibration and threshold decision record, capacity simulation, reviewer handoff form, release/rollback checklist and the explicit statement that no real renewal outcome was observed.

## Further reading

[Renewal Triage: the capacity-aware ML lab](/en/articles/renewal-triage-mlops), [score a portfolio by evidence](/en/articles/score-an-ai-portfolio-by-evidence-not-fluency) and [turn course work into an eight-week evidence sprint](/en/articles/turn-an-ai-course-into-an-eight-week-evidence-sprint).

## What should exist after the 90 seconds

Ask yourself three follow-ups: Which mechanism did I make explicit? Which trade-off or stop condition did I name? Which artefact could I open for someone to inspect? If one answer exists only in your spoken answer, add a fixed case, a short trace, a decision record, or a README section.

## Keep two kinds of evidence separate

**Technical evidence** can be an expected result for a fixed input, a versioned configuration, a test, a trace, or a rejected case. It should show where the system can fail, not only a fluent output.

**Delivery, business, and risk evidence** should say who uses the result, which decision a mistake obstructs, who takes over, and what the system deliberately does not do. Portfolio examples use synthetic data or authorised fixtures only; they do not describe a company system, a current interview process, or a business outcome.

## Scope note

This is an AI.DOG single-question practice exercise. The question, scenario, data, artefacts, and results are teaching material. Do not treat it as a company question, product behaviour, or hiring prediction.
